children: Industry headwinds that have impacted the supply of beef and production costs of chicken may be dissipating, putting Tyson Foods
on a more profitable path and earning an upgrade to Buy at J.P. Morgan.

Analyst Thomas Palmer sees the company enjoying a series of tailwinds in the beef industry (reduced operational footprint, increased domestic supply, gradual resumption of cattle imports from Mexico) and production cuts in chicken to offset higher feed costs, all of which are reasons to be optimistic on Tyson Foods.

“We appreciate that we may be slightly early on the call; however, [Tyson] shares already trade at book value, an historic support level for the shares,” Palmer writes in his note, adding that while the current earnings mix is skewed heavily toward higher multiple segments (chicken and prepared foods), Tyson shares trade at a 1x discount to historical averages on EV/EBITDA.
In addition to an upgrade from Neutral, Palmer updated his FY26 estimates to adjust for Tyson’s
earlier this month and FY27 and FY28 for weaker chicken margins due to rising feed costs, which is partially offset by improved results in its beef segment.
Palmer now sees FY26 EPS at $3.35 from $3.83, FY27 to $3.70 from $4.21, and FY28 to $4.39 from $4.90.
shares are higher in Friday’s premarket trading .

title: Tyson's beef and chicken headwinds may be dissipating -- J.P. Morgan
